title: ephemeral incident snapshot + safe-share gateway and policy-driven redaction
author: Priya Sharma
description:
Motivation: Teams frequently need to share slices of telemetry (logs, traces, lightweight flamegraphs, and metric dashboards) with third parties or cross-functional collaborators during postmortems. Current clipboard/runbook helpers either leak sensitive fields or require manual sanitization. This PR introduces an ephemeral incident snapshot generator plus a SafeShare gateway that issues time-limited signed URLs for sanitized telemetry bundles. The goal is a low-friction, auditable, and policy-driven way to create and share postmortem artifacts without shipping raw PII-sensitive data outside the org.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a new snapshot generator service (incident-bot/snapshotter) capable of producing compact bundles; implements a policy-driven redaction DSL with templates for common categories (emails, IPs, tokens, internal hostnames); adds a SafeShare gateway that issues pre-signed, short-lived URLs (default 1 hour) for download; integrates KMS-tagged packaging and audit logs; exposes a new incident-bot CLI helper and Slack action to request a sanitized snapshot; adds server-side rate limits and policy enforcement to avoid accidental mass export.

Design notes and constraints: - Sanitization is policy-first: admins can define redaction templates in /policies/redaction.yaml. Policies are evaluated server-side; the snapshot includes a manifest listing applied rules and a deterministic redaction checksum for verification. - Bundles are gzipped JSONL for logs + optional trace/minidump attachments; maximum bundle size is capped (configurable) and large attachments are replaced with a synthetic pointer to the retained crash artifact (if allowed). - SafeShare gateway returns signed URLs (HMAC v1) that are stored in short-lived internal storage and rotated via KMS. Download attempts are audited to the incident audit log service with requester identity. - Backwards compatible: old clipboard flows still work; creating a SafeShare snapshot is opt-in and requires the new RBAC permission `snapshot:share`.

Checklist (implemented): 
- [x] snapshot generator service with redaction pipeline
- [x] redaction DSL and three built-in templates (pii, secrets, infra-hostnames)
- [x] SafeShare gateway with HMAC-signed URLs and expiry enforcement
- [x] CLI command `rb-snapshot create --safe-share` and Slack action integration
- [x] audit logging and KMS envelope tags
- [x] integration tests for redaction and expiry
- [x] docs and admin migration notes

Security considerations: Default redaction templates block common PII and bearer tokens; token redaction is conservative (replaces entire header value). There is an admin override flow only available to `snapshot:override` role and gated by an approval step in the UI. All generated bundles have a tamper-evident manifest signed with the service key.

Operational notes / rollout plan: Feature is behind a feature flag `ephemeral_snapshot_safe_share`. Rollout to alpha orgs for two weeks, then gradual enable for SRE and then org-wide. Monitoring: new metrics snapshotter.requests, snapshotter.redactions.{count,by_rule}, safeshare.hits, safeshare.expired_access. Alerts for >10% redaction failures or >5 failed downloads per minute.

Tests and verification: Unit tests for parsing and redaction rule engine, integration test that generates a bundle and verifies both redaction and manifest signature, e2e test covering Slack flow and expiration. CI: all tests pass locally and in CI.

Related: ENG-4512 (policy-driven telemetry exports), SRE-2201 (postmortem sharing requirements), SUP-942 (support request that motivated conservative redaction on logs).

review_comments: Ethan Liu (2026-02-11): Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) add a TTL enforcement in the middleware not only at issuance so if storage is restored it still fails; (2) can we add a metric that counts redaction-rule matches per rule?
Author (Priya Sharma) (2026-02-12): Added TTL double-check and per-rule metrics (snapshotter.redactions.by_rule). Updated tests to assert TTL enforcement.
Marco Rivera (2026-02-13): Need to ensure RBAC check for `snapshot:share` happens before bundle render to avoid wasted CPU. Also please add an audit event for attempted overrides.
Author (Priya Sharma) (2026-02-14): Moved RBAC check earlier in the flow and added attempted_override audit event. Added a note in docs for admin reviewers.
Sophie Nguyen (2026-02-15): Docs look good. One nit: clarify that minidump attachments are trimmed unless `snapshot:attach-minidump` is present.
Ethan Liu (2026-02-16): Approving after test fixes. CI passed.
release_notes: Add an opt-in Ephemeral Snapshot and SafeShare gateway: generate sanitized, time-limited telemetry bundles for secure postmortems. Managed via redaction policies; requires `snapshot:share` permission. Feature behind feature flag; rollout notes in docs/ops/snapshots.md.
notes_for_support: If customers report missing fields after snapshot, check their redaction policy in policies/redaction.yaml. For expired links, verify system clocks between snapshotter and safeshare gateway and KMS key rotation. For large bundle failures, check bundle_size_limit in config and inspect audit logs for replacement reasons.
how_to_test_locally: 1) enable feature flag in local config; 2) run cmd/snapshotter locally; 3) create snapshot via CLI `rb-snapshot create --incident <id> --safe-share`; 4) fetch signed URL and verify download within 1 hour; 5) run tests/integration/snapshot_redaction_test.go
post_merge_tasks:
- Remove feature flag gating after canary period
- Add org-wide default redaction policy if no policy configured
- Announce in #oncall and run a short walkthrough session
impact_assessment: Low risk: new service added, opt-in by feature flag and RBAC-protected. CPU spikes possible when many large snapshots are generated; added concurrency limits and queue depth defaults. No breaking API changes.
downgrade_plan: If issues observed, flip feature flag off and delete scheduled snapshot jobs. Signed URLs will expire naturally; audit logs retained. Rollback snapshotter deployment to previous image if necessary.
examples:
CLI: rb-snapshot create --incident INC-2026-02-09 --safe-share --policy pii --ttl 3600
Slack: Use 'Create Snapshot (SafeShare)' button on incident channel and accept approval prompt
notes: This PR intentionally leaves the default TTL short (1h) and conservative redaction templates to minimize accidental data leaks. Admins can extend TTL and whitelist rules in policies/redaction.yaml under controlled roles.
